metadata.title: EcoSort AI Evidence-Based Waste Taxonomy and Knowledge Base
metadata.verification_rule: Strictly grounded in authentic government gazettes. No synthetic or AI-guessed facts.

items.item_name: Cooked Food Scraps and Meal Leftovers
items.description: Organic solid waste resulting from food preparation, leftovers from meals, dining, catering establishments, and kitchens as defined under Rule 3(zzl) of the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026.
items.segregation_instructions: Segregate at source into the designated Green Bin. Never mix with plastic wrappers, carry bags, foil, or cutlery per Rule 5(1)(b) of the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026.
items.preparation_instructions: Drain excessive liquids and gravies before depositing into the green bin to prevent anaerobic leachate formation and foul odors.
items.handling_precautions: Store in a covered, ventilated container to prevent fly infestation, animal menace, and foul odors prior to daily collection.
items.recycling_or_disposal_guidance: Processed through aerobic composting, vermi-composting, or bio-methanation (anaerobic digestion) at decentralized Micro Composting Centres (MCCs) or municipal biomethanation facilities under Rule 39(19) and Rule 39(23).
items.environmental_information: Organic waste diverted from landfills undergoes biological stabilization, preventing uncontrolled methane emissions and ground water contamination via leachate (Rule 3(q) and Schedule II).

items.description: Uncooked raw vegetable trimmings, peels, fruit skins, rinds, seeds, and spoiled produce from domestic kitchens and municipal markets as defined under Rule 3(zzl) of the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026.
items.segregation_instructions: Deposit directly into the green wet-waste container. Must not be placed inside single-use plastic carry bags per Rule 5(1)(b) and Tamil Nadu G.O. (Ms.) No. 84.
items.preparation_instructions: Remove plastic stickers, rubber bands, netting, or twist ties attached to produce before disposal.
items.handling_precautions: Keep container covered to avoid attracting fruit flies and pests.
items.recycling_or_disposal_guidance: Ideal feedstock for decentralized on-site composting, bio-gas generation, or collection for municipal Micro Composting Centres (Rule 39(19), Rule 39(23)).
items.environmental_information: High-moisture organic material that produces nutrient-rich organic compost compliant with heavy metal and stability standards in Schedule III.

items.item_name: Raw and Cooked Meat, Fish, and Poultry Scraps
items.description: Organic animal-derived waste including butcher residues, fish cleaning waste, poultry offal, and bones generated by households and market stalls under Rule 3(zzl) and Rule 39(19) of the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026.
items.segregation_instructions: Segregate as wet waste. Do not mix with dry recyclables or throw onto streets or drains per Rule 5(1)(f).
items.preparation_instructions: Drain fluids; wrap loosely in plain unprinted newspaper if required to contain odor before placing in the green bin.
items.handling_precautions: Rapidly decomposes causing strong putrefactive odors; requires daily collection by the local body.
items.recycling_or_disposal_guidance: Collected on a day-to-day basis by urban local bodies for dedicated processing in biomethanation or controlled high-rate compost plants under Rule 39(19).
items.environmental_information: Prevents vector breeding, animal scavenging, and water body pollution prohibited under Rule 5(1)(f) and Rule 39(7).

source_references.issuing_organisation: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC), Government of India

items.item_name: Spent Tea Leaves and Coffee Grounds
items.description: Biodegradable organic residue from brewed tea and coffee preparation in domestic kitchens, offices, and tea stalls.
items.segregation_instructions: Place directly into the green wet-waste bin. Separate paper or plastic composite tea bags unless certified compostable.
items.preparation_instructions: Ensure non-biodegradable synthetic mesh or staple pins from packaged tea bags are completely removed.
items.handling_precautions: Allow hot tea grounds to cool to ambient temperature before depositing in storage bins.
items.recycling_or_disposal_guidance: High-nitrogen organic soil additive, processed through vermi-composting or decentralized community composters (Rule 39(24)).
items.environmental_information: Rich in organic carbon and nitrogen, contributing to soil humus without chemical fertilizers (Rule 39(18)).

source_references.issuing_organisation: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC), Government of India

items.description: Biodegradable calcium carbonate shells generated during cooking and egg consumption.
items.segregation_instructions: Place into the green wet-waste container. Never dispose of inside plastic egg cartons or plastic carry bags.
items.preparation_instructions: Crush lightly to reduce volume in household compost or municipal collection bin.
items.handling_precautions: None; stable dry organic mineral matrix.
items.recycling_or_disposal_guidance: Provides essential calcium and structural porosity in municipal windrow and aerobic compost systems compliant with Schedule III.
items.environmental_information: Natural mineral-organic soil conditioner that buffers compost acidity.

source_references.issuing_organisation: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC), Government of India

items.description: Organic flower waste, plant leaves, garlands, and biodegradable offerings from domestic altars, places of worship, and flower markets as defined under Rule 3(zzl) and Rule 39(19).
items.segregation_instructions: Segregate as wet waste. Remove all synthetic strings, plastic packaging, incense stick plastic wrappers, and foil decorations before binning.
items.preparation_instructions: Untie synthetic threads, ribbons, or nylon twines used in floral garlands.
items.handling_precautions: Do not throw into rivers, tanks, or surface water bodies; Rule 5(1)(f) and Rule 39(7) strictly prohibit disposing of waste in water bodies.
items.recycling_or_disposal_guidance: Processed via temple compost units, municipal biomethanation, or decentralized Micro Composting Centres (Rule 39(19), Rule 39(24)).
items.environmental_information: Diverting worship flowers from water bodies prevents eutrophication and dissolved oxygen depletion in urban lakes and rivers.

source_references.issuing_organisation: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC), Government of India

items.subcategory: Street Vendor and Domestic Organic Waste
items.description: Fibrous organic husk and hard endocarp from tender coconut water consumption and cooking, explicitly identified as street vendor waste under Rule 5(1)(g) of the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026.
items.segregation_instructions: Deposit into designated organic collection containers or municipal storage depots as directed by the local body (Rule 5(1)(g)).
items.preparation_instructions: Drain residual water completely to prevent mosquito larvae breeding.
items.handling_precautions: Heavy and bulky; keep separated from fine kitchen waste to facilitate shredding.
items.recycling_or_disposal_guidance: Shredded mechanically for coir extraction, bio-compost bulking agent, or high-calorific biomass briquette manufacturing (Rule 3(o)).
items.environmental_information: High lignin content prevents rapid rotting, making it an excellent moisture-retention amendment in city compost.

source_references.issuing_organisation: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC), Government of India

items.description: Plant-based residues from domestic gardens, compound yards, and residential parks as defined under Rule 3(y) and Rule 5(1)(e) of the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026.
items.segregation_instructions: Store separately on premises and dispose of as per local authority directions (Rule 5(1)(e)). Do not mix with plastic or dry trash.
items.preparation_instructions: Large branches and heavy tree logs exceeding daily municipal collection limits must be stored separately for periodic green-waste collection.
items.handling_precautions: Burning garden leaves is strictly prohibited under Rule 5(1)(f) and subject to spot fines under Rule 39(31).
items.recycling_or_disposal_guidance: On-site backyard composting in residential premises or collection for community compost yards in municipal parks (Rule 39(22)).
items.environmental_information: Open burning of leaves releases carcinogenic polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons and particulate matter; composting returns carbon safely to soil.

source_references.issuing_organisation: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC), Government of India

items.description: Discarded newsprint, printed publications, and periodicals composed of recyclable cellulose fiber defined as recyclable dry waste under Rule 3(s) and Rule 3(zw) of the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026.
items.segregation_instructions: Segregate as dry waste into the Blue Bin. Keep completely dry and unsoiled by food, oil, or water.
items.preparation_instructions: Stack flat and bundle together. Keep free of cellophane wrapping or adhesive plastic tape.
items.handling_precautions: Store away from open flames, moisture, and water sources to preserve fiber recyclability.
items.recycling_or_disposal_guidance: Handed over to authorized waste pickers or transferred via Material Recovery Facilities (MRFs) to registered paper pulping mills (Rule 3(ze), Rule 9, Rule 39(4)).
items.environmental_information: Recycling newsprint reduces virgin tree pulp harvesting and industrial water consumption in paper manufacturing mills.

source_references.issuing_organisation: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC), Government of India

items.description: Kraft paper shipping boxes, folding carton packaging, and corrugated fiberboard containers as specified under Rule 3(s) and Rule 3(zw) of the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026.
items.segregation_instructions: Place in the Blue Dry Waste Bin or storage depot. Do not mix with wet waste or contaminated food containers.
items.preparation_instructions: Flatten or collapse all boxes to minimize storage volume; remove plastic packaging tapes and expanded polystyrene (thermocol) inserts.
items.handling_precautions: Keep dry; wet or oil-soaked cardboard cannot be recycled and turns into non-recyclable solid waste.
items.recycling_or_disposal_guidance: Baled and sorted at Material Recovery Facilities (MRFs) under Rule 9 and shipped to authorized corrugated box mills for re-pulping.
items.environmental_information: High recovery efficiency; multiple recycling cycles reduce deforestation and landfill volume.

source_references.issuing_organisation: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC), Government of India

items.description: Multi-material aseptic packaging typically composed of paperboard (approx. 70-75%), polyethylene, and aluminium foil, defined as recyclable dry packaging under Rule 3(s) and Rule 39(7).
items.segregation_instructions: Deposit into the Blue Dry Waste Bin. Prohibited from being littered in public spaces under Rule 39(7).
items.preparation_instructions: Cut open top, rinse with water to remove liquid residue, and flatten completely to prevent odors and insect infestation.
items.handling_precautions: Ensure zero foul liquid remains inside.
items.recycling_or_disposal_guidance: Sorted at Material Recovery Facilities (MRFs) and routed to specialized hydropulper recyclers to separate paper pulp from poly-aluminium (polyAl) sheets.
items.environmental_information: Reclaimed polyAl is manufactured into eco-roofing sheets, panel boards, and industrial pallets without landfilling.

source_references.issuing_organisation: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC), Government of India

items.item_name: PET Beverage and Water Bottles (Resin Code 1)
items.description: Polyethylene Terephthalate (PET) clear or tinted containers for drinking water, carbonated soft drinks, and edible oils, categorized under Category I Rigid Plastic Packaging under Plastic Waste Management Rules.
items.segregation_instructions: Place in the Blue Dry Waste Bin per Rule 39(51). Must never be littered, burned, or dumped into drains (Rule 5(1)(f)).
items.preparation_instructions: Empty all remaining liquid, remove the cap (or screw cap on tight after crushing), and flatten/crush bottle to save space.
items.handling_precautions: Do not burn; open burning of plastics generates toxic black smoke and violates Rule 5(1)(f).
items.recycling_or_disposal_guidance: Sorted and shredded into PET flakes at Material Recovery Facilities (MRFs) and sent to registered recyclers to produce recycled polyester fiber or food-grade rPET.
items.environmental_information: High circularity; PET recycling saves petroleum feedstock and lowers greenhouse gas emissions compared to virgin polymer production.

items.description: High-Density Polyethylene rigid containers commonly used for personal care products, detergents, and chemicals, covered under Category I Rigid Plastics under PWM Rules.
items.segregation_instructions: Segregate as dry waste in the Blue Bin. Ensure containers are completely drained.
items.preparation_instructions: Rinse clean of chemical or detergent residues and replace cap securely.
items.handling_precautions: Containers previously holding toxic pesticides or hazardous industrial solvents are classified as Special Care Waste under Rule 3(zx), NOT ordinary dry waste.
items.recycling_or_disposal_guidance: Aggregated at MRFs for pelletization and recycling into pipes, bins, crates, and plastic lumber by authorized plastic recyclers.
items.environmental_information: Durable thermoplastic with established recycling infrastructure across Indian industrial hubs.

items.item_name: Polypropylene Food Containers and Caps (Resin Code 5)
items.description: Polypropylene plastic items including rigid takeout containers, plastic bottle caps, buckets, and storage tubs under Rule 3(s) and PWM EPR Category I.
items.segregation_instructions: Deposit into the Blue Dry Waste Bin.
items.preparation_instructions: Rinse clean of food residues and oils; grease contamination damages recycling batch quality.
items.handling_precautions: Ensure item is free of attached metal springs or food leftovers.
items.recycling_or_disposal_guidance: Mechanical recycling into molded automotive parts, household storage buckets, and industrial pallets by registered recyclers (Rule 3(zj)).
items.environmental_information: Recycling PP reduces landfill mass and microplastic fragmentation in terrestrial and marine environments.

items.description: Low-Density Polyethylene clean flexible packaging, pallet stretch films, and air-cushion bubble packaging conforming to thickness standards.
items.segregation_instructions: Place in the Blue Dry Waste Bin. Keep clean and dry.
items.preparation_instructions: Remove paper shipping labels, packing tape, and foreign stickers where feasible.
items.handling_precautions: Do not mix with food-stained bags, wet kitchen scraps, or banned ultra-thin carry bags.
items.recycling_or_disposal_guidance: Baled at Material Recovery Facilities (MRFs) and supplied to recyclers for film-grade re-granulation or for bitumen polymer-modified road construction under CPCB guidelines.
items.environmental_information: Diverting film plastic prevents storm drain blockages and livestock ingestion.

items.description: Single-use plastic items whose manufacture, sale, and use are prohibited under MoEFCC PWM amendments (2021/2022) and Tamil Nadu G.O. (Ms.) No. 84.
items.segregation_instructions: Place in the Blue Dry Waste Bin as non-recyclable combustible dry waste. Prohibited from being littered or burned (Rule 5(1)(f)).
items.preparation_instructions: Shake clean of dirt or organic residues.
items.handling_precautions: Subject to confiscation and statutory spot fines under Tamil Nadu ULB Rules 2023 and SWM Rules Rule 39(31).
items.recycling_or_disposal_guidance: Non-recyclable combustible fraction sorted at MRFs for Refuse Derived Fuel (RDF) manufacturing or co-processing in cement kilns exceeding 1500 kcal/kg (Rule 3(l), Rule 3(o), Rule 3(zl)).
items.environmental_information: Eliminating single-use plastics stops non-degradable polymer clogging of urban waterways and aquatic wildlife mortality.

items.item_name: Multi-Layered Plastic Packaging (Chips and Snack Pouches)
items.description: Composite packaging having at least one layer of plastic in combination with other materials like aluminium foil or paper, defined as combustible waste under Rule 3(l) and PWM Category III.
items.segregation_instructions: Segregate into the Blue Dry Waste Bin. Keep separate from organic wet waste.
items.preparation_instructions: Empty all food crumbs and powders completely.
items.handling_precautions: Do not burn; open burning generates toxic dioxins and furans prohibited under Rule 5(1)(f).
items.recycling_or_disposal_guidance: Sorted at Material Recovery Facilities (MRFs) for conversion into Refuse Derived Fuel (RDF) pellets or sent for energy recovery in cement kilns and waste-to-energy plants (Rule 3(zl), Rule 3(o)).
items.environmental_information: Non-biodegradable and technically non-recyclable back into virgin polymer; regulated through brand-owner EPR obligations.

items.description: Non-ferrous aluminium containers and clean aluminium domestic foil, defined as recyclable dry waste under Rule 3(s) and Rule 3(zw) of the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026.
items.segregation_instructions: Deposit in the Blue Dry Waste Bin. Do not litter on streets or open spaces (Rule 39(7)).
items.preparation_instructions: Rinse beverage cans clean and crush flat to optimize storage density. Wipe greasy foils.
items.handling_precautions: Smooth sharp cut edges of torn cans to prevent injury to waste handlers.
items.recycling_or_disposal_guidance: Sorted at MRFs and supplied to secondary aluminium smelters for infinite recycling without loss of metallurgical properties (Rule 3(zj)).
items.environmental_information: Recycling aluminium saves up to 95% of the electrical energy required to extract primary metal from bauxite ore.

source_references.issuing_organisation: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC), Government of India

items.description: Ferrous tin-coated steel cans and metal lids used for preserved foods, paints (clean), and edible oils under Rule 3(s) and Rule 3(zw).
items.segregation_instructions: Place in the Blue Dry Waste Bin.
items.preparation_instructions: Rinse out food remains; press the opened lid inside the can to prevent jagged edges.
items.handling_precautions: Take care with sharp edges.
items.recycling_or_disposal_guidance: Magnetic separation at MRFs (Rule 9) followed by shipment to steel electric arc furnaces and foundries for smelting into new steel products.
items.environmental_information: Ferrous scrap has a mature industrial circular economy in India, preserving iron ore reserves.

source_references.issuing_organisation: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC), Government of India

items.item_name: Intact Glass Bottles and Food Jars
items.description: Clean, uncracked flint (clear), amber, and green soda-lime glass containers under Rule 3(s) and Rule 3(zw) of the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026.
examples: soft drink and juice glass bottles
items.segregation_instructions: Place gently into the Blue Dry Waste Bin or dedicated glass collection box.
items.preparation_instructions: Empty contents, rinse interior with water, and remove metal/plastic screw caps (sort caps into respective metal/plastic streams).
items.handling_precautions: Handle carefully to avoid breakage; broken glass poses severe laceration hazards to waste pickers.
items.recycling_or_disposal_guidance: Color-sorted (cullet) at MRFs and melted in industrial glass furnaces into new bottles indefinitely without quality degradation (Rule 3(zj)).
items.environmental_information: Glass is 100% recyclable; cullet lowers furnace melting temperatures, cutting energy use and carbon emissions.

source_references.issuing_organisation: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC), Government of India

items.description: Fragmented or shattered glass containers, broken tumblers, and fractured flat glass requiring careful containment.
items.segregation_instructions: Segregate as dry waste, but NEVER throw loose into the dry bin.
items.preparation_instructions: Wrap securely in thick cardboard, multiple sheets of newspaper, or place inside an intact cardboard box marked 'BROKEN GLASS' before handing over.
items.handling_precautions: Extreme laceration hazard; protective puncture-proof gloves mandated for waste workers under Rule 39(29).
items.recycling_or_disposal_guidance: Cullet recycled in commercial glass kilns or processed as an aggregate additive in industrial tile / asphalt manufacturing.
items.environmental_information: Containment protects sanitary workers and waste pickers from physical injury and occupational infections.

source_references.issuing_organisation: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC), Government of India

items.item_name: Discarded Textiles and Clean Old Clothing
items.description: Worn-out apparel, clean bedsheets, cloth cuttings, and natural/synthetic fabric remnants categorized as dry non-biodegradable waste under Rule 3(s).
items.segregation_instructions: Place in the Blue Dry Waste Bin or donate usable clothing via community thrift drives.
items.preparation_instructions: Ensure textiles are dry and clean. Do not mix with oil rags or chemically soiled cleaning cloths.
items.handling_precautions: Keep away from wet kitchen waste to avoid fungal mold and mildew growth.
items.recycling_or_disposal_guidance: Shredded for mechanical yarn recycling, industrial wiping rags, sound insulation batting, or used in RDF production if synthetic and non-recyclable (Rule 3(zl)).
items.environmental_information: Extending fabric life diverts significant volume from landfills and reduces agricultural water footprint of virgin cotton.

source_references.issuing_organisation: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC), Government of India

items.item_name: Inert Dust, Street Sweepings, and Drain Silt
items.description: Non-biodegradable, non-recyclable, and non-combustible street sweeping dust, grit, and silt removed from surface drains as defined in Rule 3(z) of the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026.
items.segregation_instructions: Collected separately by local bodies; prohibited from being mixed with wet waste under Rule 39(33).
items.preparation_instructions: Temporary storage in covered secondary storage depots per Rule 39(21).
items.handling_precautions: Prohibited from being mixed with organic wet waste or dumped in unauthorized open plots (Rule 39(2)(xi), Rule 39(33)).
items.recycling_or_disposal_guidance: Permitted for safe disposal at engineered sanitary landfills meeting Schedule II specifications or used as daily soil cover at landfills (Rule 39(49), Schedule II).
items.environmental_information: Preventing road dust mixing preserves wet waste compost purity according to heavy metal limits in Schedule III.

source_references.issuing_organisation: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC), Government of India
source_references.rule_or_section: Rule 3(z), Rule 39(21), Rule 39(33), Rule 39(49), Schedule II

items.description: Used diapers comprising absorbent cellulose fluff, superabsorbent polymers (SAP), polyolefin films, and human excretory matter, explicitly defined under Rule 3(zp) and Rule 3(zq) of the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026.
items.segregation_instructions: Must be segregated at source in the third dedicated sanitary stream. Mandatorily wrapped securely in pouches provided by manufacturers or wrapping material instructed by local bodies, and placed in a dedicated sanitary bin (Rule 5(1)(c)).
items.preparation_instructions: Roll diaper inward with tapes fastened; place inside disposal pouch or heavy paper wrapper before binning.
items.handling_precautions: Biological pathogen hazard; never mix with wet compostable waste or dry recyclable plastics (Rule 5(1)(c)).
items.recycling_or_disposal_guidance: Channelized by local bodies for environmentally sound destruction in dedicated high-temperature incinerators or through Common Bio-medical Waste Treatment Facilities (CBWTF) under Rule 39(2)(xii) and Rule 8(f).
items.environmental_information: Proper high-temperature incineration destroys enteric pathogens (E. coli, Salmonella) preventing ground water and fecal-oral disease transmission.

source_references.issuing_organisation: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC), Government of India
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC), Government of India

items.description: Used sanitary towels, menstrual pads, and panty liners soiled with blood and bodily fluids, explicitly defined as sanitary waste under Rule 3(zp) of the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026.
items.segregation_instructions: Segregate into a dedicated sanitary container or red bin in public restrooms. Mandatorily wrapped securely in pouches provided by brand owners or suitable wrapping material per Rule 5(1)(c) and Rule 39(51).
items.preparation_instructions: Wrap securely in the disposal wrapper pouch provided by the manufacturer or in plain newspaper marked with a red dot/symbol as instructed by local health guidelines.
items.handling_precautions: Blood-borne pathogen vector; strictly prohibited from being thrown into toilet commodes, drains, or mixed with dry waste.
items.recycling_or_disposal_guidance: Processed through dedicated local body incinerators operating at specified combustion temperatures or Common Bio-medical Waste Treatment Facilities (CBWTF) under Rule 39(2)(xii).
items.environmental_information: Flushing sanitary pads causes catastrophic sewer blockages; open dumping exposes waste pickers to hepatitis and infectious agents.

source_references.issuing_organisation: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC), Government of India

items.description: Internal absorbent menstrual items composed of rayon/cotton fibers and plastic/cardboard insertion applicators, defined as sanitary waste under Rule 3(zp).
items.segregation_instructions: Place in dedicated sanitary waste bins. Wrap securely before binning (Rule 5(1)(c)).
items.preparation_instructions: Wrap in manufacturer pouch or toilet tissue paper securely.
items.handling_precautions: Never flush down plumbing; non-dispersible fibers cause severe drain clogs.
items.recycling_or_disposal_guidance: High-temperature thermal destruction at authorized incinerators or CBWTF units under Rule 39(2)(xii).
items.environmental_information: Thermal destruction converts infectious organic matter to sterile ash compliant with emission limits in Schedule III.

source_references.issuing_organisation: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC), Government of India

items.description: Used natural rubber latex or polyurethane barrier prophylactics contaminated with bodily fluids, classified as sanitary waste under Rule 3(zp) and Rule 3(zq).
items.segregation_instructions: Place in the sanitary waste bin separate from dry recyclables and wet compostables (Rule 5(1)(c)).
items.preparation_instructions: Tie a knot at open end; wrap in paper or disposal wrapper before binning.
items.handling_precautions: Bodily fluid contact risk; do not flush in toilets.
items.recycling_or_disposal_guidance: Thermal treatment in municipal or biomedical waste incinerators under Rule 39(2)(xii).
items.environmental_information: Synthetic additives in latex prevent rapid biodegradability in septic tanks; improper disposal pollutes aquatic ecosystems.

source_references.issuing_organisation: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC), Government of India

items.item_name: Disposable Incontinence Underpads and Bed Sheets
items.description: Disposable fluid-absorbing sheets used for medical convalescence, elderly care, and incontinence management, defined under Rule 3(zp) and Rule 3(zq).
items.segregation_instructions: Fold soiled surface inward, roll tightly, wrap in paper or plastic disposal pouch, and deposit into the sanitary waste stream (Rule 5(1)(c)).
items.preparation_instructions: Fold into compact bundle with impermeable backing outward.
items.handling_precautions: Potential pathogen contamination; gloves recommended when changing and bundling.
items.recycling_or_disposal_guidance: Dedicated collection for Common Bio-medical Waste Treatment Facilities or approved incinerators under Rule 39(2)(xii).
items.environmental_information: Prevents biological contamination of recyclables and spread of hospital-acquired or domestic infections.

source_references.issuing_organisation: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC), Government of India

items.item_name: Discarded Paint Cans and Solvent Drums
items.description: Metal or plastic containers containing residues of synthetic enamels, oil paints, lacquers, thinners, and varnishes, explicitly designated as Special Care Waste under Rule 3(zx) of the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026.
items.segregation_instructions: Must be segregated separately at source as Special Care Waste. Never place into the Blue dry recyclable bin or Green wet bin (Rule 5(1)(b)).
items.preparation_instructions: Ensure lids are securely sealed to prevent volatile vapor emission or chemical leakage.
items.handling_precautions: Flammable and toxic volatile organic compounds (VOCs); keep away from heat sources and open flames.
items.recycling_or_disposal_guidance: Must be handed over to special care collection vehicles or deposited at municipal Deposition Centres established at least one per 5 sq. km under Rule 39(48) for transfer to authorized hazardous waste processors.
items.environmental_information: Contains heavy metal pigments (lead, chromium) and aromatic hydrocarbons that contaminate soil and ground water if landfilled.

source_references.issuing_organisation: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC), Government of India

items.item_name: Pesticide Cans, Insecticide Sprays, and Bottles
items.description: Aerosol cans, plastic bottles, and tins containing residues of household insecticides, mosquito sprays, termite chemicals, and garden pesticides defined under Rule 3(zx) of the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026.
items.segregation_instructions: Segregate as Special Care Waste. Do not puncture aerosol cans or mix with general household trash (Rule 5(1)(b)).
items.preparation_instructions: Keep cap on; do not wash or rinse pesticide residues into domestic household sinks or drains.
items.handling_precautions: Pressurized aerosols risk explosion if punctured or incinerated; toxic active ingredients (pyrethroids, organophosphates) absorb through skin.
items.recycling_or_disposal_guidance: Hand over to authorized hazardous waste collection infrastructure or municipal Deposition Centres (Rule 39(48)) for high-temperature hazardous waste incineration.
items.environmental_information: Rinsing pesticide containers into drains pollutes urban water bodies and kills aquatic biodiversity.

source_references.issuing_organisation: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC), Government of India

items.item_name: Compact Fluorescent Lamps (CFLs) and Tube Lights
items.description: Spent compact fluorescent lamps (CFLs), linear fluorescent tube lights, and high-intensity discharge lamps containing toxic elemental mercury vapor, explicitly designated as Special Care Waste under Rule 3(zx) of SWM Rules 2026.
items.segregation_instructions: Segregate strictly into Special Care Waste. Never discard into regular dry waste bins or smash in open air (Rule 5(1)(b)).
items.preparation_instructions: Store intact in original cardboard sleeves or bubble wrap to prevent accidental breakage during transit.
items.handling_precautions: If broken, evacuate room for 15 minutes to disperse mercury vapor; do not vacuum; sweep shards with stiff paper while wearing gloves.
items.recycling_or_disposal_guidance: Delivered to municipal Deposition Centres (Rule 39(48)) or authorized e-waste/hazardous recyclers equipped with mercury-retort distillation recovery systems.
items.environmental_information: Mercury bioaccumulates as toxic methylmercury in aquatic food chains, causing severe neurological disorders.

source_references.issuing_organisation: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC), Government of India

items.description: Glass clinical fever thermometers and barometers containing liquid elemental mercury, explicitly classified as Special Care Waste under Rule 3(zx) of the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026.
items.segregation_instructions: Segregate immediately into the Special Care Waste stream (Rule 5(1)(b)).
items.preparation_instructions: Place intact or broken thermometer and spilled mercury beads into an airtight glass jar with a small amount of water or sealed plastic container.
items.handling_precautions: Never touch mercury beads with bare hands; never vacuum or pour mercury down the drain.
items.recycling_or_disposal_guidance: Hand over to municipal Deposition Centres (Rule 39(48)) or Common Bio-medical Waste Treatment Facilities equipped for hazardous mercury containment.
items.environmental_information: 1 gram of elemental mercury can contaminate a 20-acre lake; proper collection prevents neurotoxic environmental contamination.

items.description: Date-expired, damaged, or unconsumed pharmaceutical drugs, antibiotic tablets, capsules, medicated syrups, and ointments under Rule 3(zx) of the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026.
items.segregation_instructions: Segregate as Special Care Waste. Never flush down toilets, pour into kitchen sinks, or mix with food waste (Rule 5(1)(f)).
items.preparation_instructions: Keep in original blister strips or bottles; do not crush tablets together.
items.handling_precautions: Keep out of reach of children and domestic pets; prevent diversion into informal counterfeit markets.
items.recycling_or_disposal_guidance: Collected through municipal Deposition Centres (Rule 39(48)) or pharmacy take-back kiosks for high-temperature incineration at authorized CBWTFs.
items.environmental_information: Flushing antibiotics and active pharmaceutical ingredients into sewers creates multi-drug antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in municipal water supplies.

items.item_name: Household Medical Needles, Syringes, and Sharps
items.description: Used diabetic insulin needles, disposable plastic syringes, lancets, and finger-prick blades generated during self-administered healthcare at home, defined under Rule 3(zx) of SWM Rules 2026.
items.segregation_instructions: Strictly segregate as Special Care Waste. Never mix with ordinary dry plastics or wet waste (Rule 5(1)(b)).
items.preparation_instructions: Must be contained in a puncture-proof, rigid plastic container (e.g., heavy detergent bottle with secure screw cap) clearly marked 'SHARPS'. Do not recap needles manually.
items.handling_precautions: Severe needlestick injury and blood-borne virus transmission hazard (HIV, Hepatitis B/C) to waste pickers and municipal sweepers.
items.recycling_or_disposal_guidance: Deposited at municipal Deposition Centres (Rule 39(48)) and transferred to Common Bio-medical Waste Treatment Facilities (CBWTF) for autoclaving/shredding and high-temperature incineration under BMW Rules 2016.
items.environmental_information: Puncture-proof containment completely eliminates occupational needlestick injuries among sanitation workers.

items.item_name: Contaminated Medical Gauze and Wound Dressings
items.description: Cotton swabs, surgical tape, bandages, and gauze contaminated with human blood, bodily fluids, or purulent exudates generated at home, specified under Rule 3(zx) of the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026.
items.segregation_instructions: Segregate as Special Care Waste. Do not combine with dry recyclables or home compost bins (Rule 5(1)(b)).
items.preparation_instructions: Wrap securely in a sealed leak-proof plastic or paper pouch before placing in the designated special care container.
items.handling_precautions: Biohazard contact risk; handle with gloves and wash hands thoroughly with soap.
items.recycling_or_disposal_guidance: Transferred via local body Deposition Centres to Common Bio-medical Waste Treatment Facilities (CBWTF) for high-temperature bio-incineration under Rule 8(f) and BMW Rules 2016.
items.environmental_information: Incineration at >= 1050 deg C ensures complete destruction of biological pathogens and avoids open vector transmission.

items.item_name: Dry Cell and Alkaline Household Batteries
items.description: Spent primary (non-rechargeable) portable batteries including AA, AAA, C, D, and 9V zinc-carbon and alkaline cells governed under Battery Waste Management Rules, 2022 and SWM Rules 2026 Rule 3(zx).
items.segregation_instructions: Segregate strictly into Special Care / Battery Waste. Strictly prohibited from municipal solid waste bins and landfilling under Battery Waste Management Rules, 2022 Rule 4.
items.preparation_instructions: Tape the positive terminals of 9V and coin batteries with non-conductive electrical tape to prevent accidental short-circuits during storage.
items.handling_precautions: Do not mix with damp trash; corroded batteries leak caustic potassium hydroxide electrolyte.
items.recycling_or_disposal_guidance: Deposit at designated battery collection points, buy-back kiosks, or municipal Deposition Centres (Rule 39(48)) for transport to CPCB-registered battery recycling facilities.
items.environmental_information: Battery recycling recovers zinc, manganese, and steel while preventing heavy metal leaching into ground water reservoirs.

items.description: Secondary rechargeable lithium-ion cells, lithium-polymer packs from electronics, and alkaline/silver-oxide button cells from watches and hearing aids.
items.segregation_instructions: Segregate as Special Care Waste. Strictly prohibited from municipal garbage bins, open burning, or general landfill disposal under Battery Waste Management Rules 2022.
items.preparation_instructions: Cover metal terminals with non-conductive tape. Place damaged or swollen cells into individual plastic bags surrounded by sand or vermiculite.
items.handling_precautions: Thermal runaway and fire hazard: punctured, crushed, or short-circuited lithium batteries catch fire violently.
items.recycling_or_disposal_guidance: Deposit into EPR producer collection bins at authorized electronics stores or municipal Deposition Centres for processing by registered hydrometallurgical recyclers.
items.environmental_information: Recovers critical strategic elements: cobalt, lithium, nickel, and copper while eliminating high-temperature fire incidents at waste facilities.

items.item_name: Discarded USB Cables, Power Cords, and Chargers
items.description: Discarded copper-conductor charging cables, mobile power adapters, peripheral extension cords, and computer wires governed under E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2022 and SWM Rules 2026 Rule 3(zy).
items.segregation_instructions: Segregate as E-Waste / Special Care stream. Do not discard with general dry waste or burn under Rule 6 of E-Waste Rules 2022.
items.preparation_instructions: Coil cables neatly; do not strip PVC insulation at home.
items.handling_precautions: Open burning of PVC insulation releases toxic hydrochloric acid gas and persistent dioxins.
items.recycling_or_disposal_guidance: Channelize to authorized e-waste collection kiosks, producer take-back centers, or municipal Deposition Centres (Rule 8(ii)) for mechanical cable granulators that separate pure copper from PVC.
items.environmental_information: Prevents open burning by informal wire-scrappers, eliminating atmospheric release of toxic chlorinated compounds.

items.item_name: Discarded Mobile Phones, Tablets, and PCBs
items.description: Obsolete, unrepairable, or discarded cellular smartphones, tablet devices, and bare printed circuit boards (PCBs) governed under Schedule I of E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2022.
items.segregation_instructions: Store separately from household trash; deposit only through registered e-waste collection channels (Rule 6).
items.preparation_instructions: Perform factory data reset where operable, remove external memory cards and SIM cards; do not smash or shatter display screen.
items.handling_precautions: Integrated lithium battery presents fire hazard if crushed or mechanically perforated.
items.recycling_or_disposal_guidance: Channelized through registered dismantlers and recyclers using eco-friendly hydrometallurgical refining to recover gold, silver, copper, and palladium (Rule 6, Rule 13).
items.environmental_information: Formal e-waste recycling prevents acid-bath cyanide leaching and hazardous lead/cadmium soil contamination.

items.description: Small discarded electrical and electronic consumer appliances consisting of electric motors, heating elements, wiring, and plastic casings governed under Schedule I of E-Waste Rules 2022.
items.segregation_instructions: Store in dry place; hand over through e-waste drop-off kiosks, producer take-back schemes, or municipal deposition centers.
items.preparation_instructions: Clean out food/water residues from kettles or toasters; bundle appliance power cord.
items.handling_precautions: Do not dismantle components without professional personal protective equipment.
items.recycling_or_disposal_guidance: Dismantled at authorized facilities into metal scrap, engineering plastics (ABS/polycarbonate), and wiring for registered recycling (Rule 6).
items.environmental_information: Recovers steel, copper windings, and engineering polymers, keeping bulky electro-mechanical equipment out of landfills.
